title: How drones fly
examples: What makes a drone stay in the air?
How do the propellers control the movement?
Can you explain the balance needed for flying?

explain.say: A drone uses four propellers to fly through the air.
The propellers spin to create a force called lift.
To stay still, the lift must perfectly balance the drone's weight.
To move forward, the drone tilts slightly using its propellers.
If the drone needs to turn left, it changes the power of some propellers.
In real life, drones use these principles to deliver packages.

faq.q: How does the drone know when to stop moving?
faq.a: Drones use sensors to measure their position and balance. They constantly adjust the propeller speeds to maintain stability.

faq.q: If I change the propeller size, will it fly differently?
faq.a: Yes, propeller size affects how much lift the drone can generate. Bigger propellers can move more air, but they might also be slower.
asks: Does propeller size matter for lift?
What is the relationship between prop size and lift?

faq.q: Does the drone need batteries to fly?
faq.a: Yes, the motors and propellers need electrical power from batteries to spin. The battery supplies the energy for the lift.
asks: Can a drone fly without electricity?

faq.q: Is the balance the same for all drones?
faq.a: No, the balance system must be calibrated for the drone's weight and size. A heavier drone needs more powerful motors to balance.

faq.q: Do all drones use four propellers?
faq.a: While many common models use four, some larger or specialized drones might use more or fewer propellers depending on their design.
asks: Must a drone have four propellers?
Are there other propeller counts for drones?

facts: Drones create lift by spinning propellers to push air downwards.
To hover, the upward lift force must equal the downward force of gravity.
Changing the power to different propellers allows the drone to turn or move.
Tilt is used to direct the thrust, causing the drone to move in a direction.

quiz.say: What must be true for a drone to hover perfectly still?

options.show: Lift must be greater than Weight
options.say: Lift must be greater than Weight

quiz.why: When the upward lift force equals the downward weight, the drone remains balanced and stationary.

wrong.1: This would cause the drone to accelerate upwards, not hover.
wrong.2: The drone still has its own weight, which must be supported by the lift.
wrong.3: The propellers need to spin continuously to generate the necessary lift force.

quiz.say: If a drone wants to move straight forward, what must it do?

options.show: Spin the propellers faster on one side
options.say: Spin the propellers faster on one side

options.show: Increase the speed of all propellers
options.say: Increase the speed of all propellers

quiz.why: Tilting the drone changes the angle of the thrust, directing some of the lift force into forward motion.

wrong.0: This action would cause the drone to turn, not move straight ahead.
wrong.1: Decreasing lift would cause the drone to fall, not move forward.
wrong.3: Increasing speed only increases lift, causing it to rise, not move forward.

quiz.say: If the drone needs to turn to its right, which propellers must receive more power?

options.show: All propellers must get less power
options.say: All propellers must get less power

options.show: The front propellers must get more power
options.say: The front propellers must get more power

options.show: The left propellers must get more power
options.say: The left propellers must get more power

options.show: The right propellers must get more power
options.say: The right propellers must get more power

quiz.why: To turn right, the drone must pitch its body to the right, which requires more thrust from the left side propellers.

wrong.0: Reducing all power would cause the drone to fall to the ground.
wrong.1: Powering only the front propellers would cause the drone to pitch forward, not turn.
wrong.3: This would cause the drone to turn to the left, the opposite of the goal.
